s: Which of the following best describes the concept of an ecosystem?
o: A community of living organisms interacting with their physical environment
A group of the same species living in a specific area
The process of energy flow through different trophic levels
The rate of biomass production in a given area
x: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with their physical (non-living) environment. One species in an area is a population; energy flow and biomass production are functions, not the definition.

s: Which of the following is a complete, closed and independent ecosystem?
x:
Printed source gave no key. Strictly, no ecosystem is closed for energy; 'lake' is keyed as the self-sufficient natural ecosystem (NCERT: pond = self-sustainable unit).

s: Carbon and energy requirements of the autotrophic organism are fulfilled by ______.

s: Choose the correct statement.
o: Producers in an aquatic ecosystem are green plants
Archea are a type of producers who use energy from chemical compounds
Consumers are heterotrophs able to produce their food
The stability of ecosystem depends on consumers
x: Archaea such as methanogens are chemoautotrophic producers using energy from chemical compounds. Aquatic producers are mostly algae and phytoplankton, consumers cannot make food, and stability does not rest on consumers.

s: The Organisms which can tolerate a small temperature range are called:
x: Stenothermal organisms tolerate only a narrow temperature range; eurythermal ones a wide range. Psychrophiles love cold, poikilotherms vary body temperature.

s: Which one is considered as a dynamic part of an ecosystem?
x: The food chain, through which energy and matter keep moving, is the dynamic part of an ecosystem. Producers and decomposers are structural parts and atmospheric pressure is an abiotic factor.

s: Among the biotic components of the ecosystem, the producer system is –
x: Green plants are the producers (autotrophs) among the biotic components. Cow, peacock and tiger are consumers.

s: Work as intermediaries between biotic and abiotic components
x:
Official key / printed books: (c) Producers. Many textbooks also call decomposers the link between biotic and abiotic components (NextGen Environment APPSC Part 1.2 p.6).
Per the official key, producers are the intermediaries: they take in abiotic materials (CO2, water, sunlight) and turn them into food for the biotic world. Many books also describe decomposers as the link, but the key is producers.

s: The process by which plants synthesize their food is called:
x: Plants make their food by photosynthesis, using sunlight to build organic matter. Osmosis, respiration and plasmolysis are not food-making processes.

s: Photosynthesis using the invisible part of the sunlight is done by some –
x: Some bacteria, such as green sulphur bacteria, photosynthesise using invisible infrared light. Trees and algae use visible light and fungi do not photosynthesise.

s: Work as intermediaries between biotic and abiotic components :
x:
Official key / printed books: (c) Producers. Many textbooks also call decomposers the link between biotic and abiotic components (NextGen Environment APPSC Part 1.2 p.6).
Per the official key, producers are the intermediaries between abiotic materials and the biotic world, since they convert CO2, water and sunlight into food. Decomposers are also often called a link, but the key is producers.

s: The process of breaking down organic matter by microorganisms is called :
x: Breaking down organic matter by microorganisms is decomposition. Fermentation is one particular anaerobic process; respiration and photosynthesis are not breakdown of dead matter.

s: Light energy changes into the chemical energy by which of the following process :
x: Photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy stored in food. Electrolysis and respiration do not.

s: Which one of the following concerns soil?
x: Edaphic factors concern the soil (texture, pH, minerals, drainage). Climatic, biotic and topographic factors are other types.

s:
With reference to the planet Earth, consider the following statements :
I. Rain forests produce more oxygen than that produced by oceans.
II. Marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria produce about 50% of world's oxygen.
III. Well-oxygenated surface water contains several folds higher oxygen than that in atmospheric air.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: None of the above statements is correct
x: Only II is right: marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria give about half of the world's oxygen. I is wrong (oceans out-produce rainforests) and III is wrong (air holds far more oxygen than water).

s: Biodegradable wastes can usually be converted into useful substance with the help of :
x: Biodegradable wastes are broken down into useful substances such as compost by bacteria (and fungi). Viruses, nuclear proteins and radioactive substances do not do this.

s: Frogs are cold-blooded animals –
x: Frogs are cold-blooded (poikilothermic): their body temperature follows the surroundings, like snakes, lizards and fish.

s: Most of the oxygen on Earth is produced by :
x: Most of Earth's oxygen is produced by algae, mainly marine phytoplankton. Grasses, trees and paddy fields give much less.

s: Which of the following has the maximum efficiency to convert solar energy into chemical energy ?
x: Chlorella, a green alga, converts solar energy into chemical energy with very high efficiency. Tiger and earthworm are consumers and Cuscuta is a parasite without chlorophyll.

s: A biological community in its environment such as a pond, an ocean, forest, even an aquarium is known as
x: A biological community together with its environment, such as a pond, ocean, forest or aquarium, is an ecosystem. A community alone lacks the abiotic part; a biome is a large climatic region.

s:
Consider the following statement regarding ecosystem.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: I and II are correct: Tansley coined 'ecosystem' and organisms that make their own food are autotrophs. Consumers do not photosynthesise, and decomposers turn organic matter into inorganic, not the reverse.

s: Which one of the following is the best description of the term 'ecosystem'?
o: A community of organisms interacting with one another
That part of the Earth which is inhabited by living organisms
A community of organisms together with the environment in which they live
The flora and fauna of a geographical area
x: An ecosystem is a community of organisms together with the environment in which they live. Organisms interacting only = community; inhabited part of Earth = biosphere; flora and fauna = biota.

s: The term ‘Ecosystem’ was proposed by
x: The term ecosystem was proposed by A.G. Tansley in 1935. Taylor, Hartigan and Stoddart are geographers.

s: Which of the following is not a biotic component of an ecosystem?
x: Air is an abiotic (non-living) component; plants, bacteria and animals are biotic.

s: Which of the following is an artificial ecosystem?
x: A crop field is an artificial (man-modified) ecosystem. Ponds and forests are natural ecosystems.

s: In ecosystem terminology, who are the major producers in a terrestrial ecosystem?
x: In terrestrial ecosystems the producers are herbaceous and woody plants; phytoplankton are aquatic producers and humans are consumers.

Photosynthesis needs light, not a time of day: normally sunlight, but plants also photosynthesise under artificial light and some algae under moonlight, hence the key 'day or night'.
